correctness.rationale: The support identity follows from the six square facets (area 2 each) and eight hexagonal facets (area 3\(\sqrt3\) each) via Cauchy projection. The 32-vector support system is exact. Signed permutations of (14,2,2) have squared norm 204, precisely 24 nearest pairs with dot 196 and 12 second-nearest pairs with dot 188. Cap intersections are therefore absent for brightness at least 10\(\sqrt2\), and precisely those 24 pairs contribute for 14 to 10\(\sqrt2\). Spherical Gauss--Bonnet yields the explicit lens formula. Local tangent-plane expansions at the 24 cap tangencies yield the three-halves coefficient; 12 minimizers and a direct planar cone-area calculation yield the quadratic lower coefficient. An independent projected-vertex convex-hull area implementation agreed at 800 directions; 300,000 Haar draws matched the CDF branch values, and the cusp limit was numerically corroborated. These finite checks support but are not premises of the proof.

value.rationale: The Archimedean truncated octahedron is the distinguished space-tiling, 14-faced area minimizer in recent parallelohedron research; orientation-dependent shadow area is a directly motivated stereological observable. The exact nontrivial 24-cap arrangement identifies a maximal interval occupying about 11.8 percent of random views with uniform brightness density, an additional explicit spherical-lens branch, and rigorously different endpoint exponents 3/2 and 2. This gives an exact calibration law for a natural solid rather than an arbitrary numerical slice. It requires a non-obvious 32-vector projection-body reduction, exact cap adjacency counting, and tangent-cone calculations; the classical mean and generic coarea method alone do not produce the evaluated constants.
